_comment: lifeboats: big hulls launch lifeboats (more of the crew get off, longer air, and they crawl towards the nearest friendly planet) instead of escape pods. aiRunAllowed: false for ships that carry people (settlers, troops), which always have a crew. Ship classes and combat numbers. Speeds in Mm per hour (600 Mm/h is about 167 km/s), acceleration in Mm per hour per hour (15 is about 0.12 g), ranges in Mm (1 Mm = 1000 km). Supplies are the one stock of fuel and ammo; each 1 Mm/h of speed gained or lost burns suppliesPerDeltaV, each railgun shot burns suppliesPerShot. Missiles are counted on their own and reloaded at home.
_fittingComment: Fitting. Each class has slots: W weapon, D defence, U utility, E engine. A pair slot is two mirrored mounts that always carry the same module (its numbers count twice). fit is the slot's standard module (blank: empty); the class numbers above are for the standard fit, and other modules add or take away the difference. A fit must stay inside the hull's power and heat budgets (each module's power and heat, pairs twice). Modules with needs wait for that research. Refits happen at your shipyard and cost the new module's Industry. New ships get the side's saved design for the class, else the standard fit, with the best engine researched.

classes.name: Escort
classes.role: Small, cheap point defence picket. Screens bigger ships from missiles.

classes.name: Gun frigate
classes.role: Fast and cheap, short legs. Railgun pair and point defence: strong up close.

classes.name: Missile destroyer
classes.role: Long range, slower. Missile racks (4 salvos of 4) and point defence.

classes.name: Cruiser
classes.role: Big gun platform: two railgun pairs, missiles, shields and two point defence pairs. Slow and easy to see.

classes.name: Tanker
classes.role: Supply ship: carries fuel and ammunition out to fleets.

classes.name: Supply tender
classes.role: Small supply ship, no research needed: a little fuel, ammunition and food. Keeps up with frigates, so it can sail with a fleet, or haul goods between nearby worlds.

classes.name: Freighter
classes.role: Supply ship: carries food out to fleets.

classes.name: Picket
classes.role: Small sensor ship: sees far and is hard to spot. Spots for a fleet.

classes.name: Siege monitor
classes.role: Heavy railguns and armour on a very slow hull: breaks blockades and shipyards.

classes.name: Capital ship
classes.role: The biggest gun platform: three railgun pairs, missiles, heavy shields. Costly and slow; losing one hurts.

classes.name: Bulk freighter
classes.role: Twice a freighter's cargo, slow. Best on safe runs.

classes.name: Settler ship
classes.role: Built by a settle order: carries up to 10k settlers to one planet, lands, and is gone.

classes.name: Troop ship
classes.role: Carries 2k troops raised from a planet you hold: lands them from low orbit to take a planet, or boards a ship on an enemy slipway.

_modulesComment: materials: what the part takes to build beyond the hull (a ship costs its class materials, which cover the standard fit, plus the parts it adds minus the standard parts it leaves out). cargo: hold space the part takes. hidden: a concealed mount that enemy sensors can't see until it fires (Concealed mounts research). Modules for the slots. Each adds its numbers to the ship (pairs twice) and uses power and heat from the hull's budgets. accelFactor multiplies thrust; burnHeatFactor multiplies the heat a burn makes. cost is Industry, paid at a refit. fuels: what the engine can burn (with fuel types on); the first is its usual fuel.
_fuelsComment: Fuel types (a game-start switch; off, every engine burns the one 'fuel' good). Each fuel is a good. thrust multiplies acceleration, reach divides the supplies a burn takes (more speed change per tank), burnHeat multiplies the heat of a burn, signature multiplies how bright a burn shows on enemy sensors, perSupply is the good used per supply unit put in a tank (rarer fuels go further per unit). Refuelling with no stock of any fuel the engine burns goes at noFuelRefill pace; only water can be scraped together anywhere. A ship carries one fuel at a time: switching hands what is left back to the planet's store.

fuels.name: Hydrogen + oxygen
fuels.note: Strong kick for dodges and launches; poor reach

fuels.name: Water
fuels.note: Cheap and everywhere; weak. Fine for freighters and short hops

fuels.name: Fission pellets
fuels.note: Long reach; the core runs very hot, so a long burn needs radiators out

fuels.name: Deuterium
fuels.note: Fusion reach at moderate heat. Needs the fusion drive

fuels.name: Helium-3
fuels.note: Best reach, cool and clean burn. Rare: worth raiding for

fuels.name: Antimatter
fuels.note: Everything at once, at a huge price

_rangesComment: Reach, longest first: contact (battle time) 100,000 km, missile launch 60,000 km, railguns 40,000 km (hits fall off with range, so fleets that engage close to engageRangeMm x 0.75), point defence 12,000 km (last-ditch, inside railgun reach). Railgun slugs fly at slugSpeedMmPerHour (250 km/s) plus the closing speed.

combat._flagBridgeComment: With light lag on, the fleet carrying the flagship fights better: railguns reload in reloadFactor of the time, point defence kills pointDefenceFactor times as many missiles (linked fire control), and railgun hit chances are accuracyFactor times higher (fire control spreads shots over the targets).
combat._dodgeComment: A fleet set to dodge sidesteps railgun fire: each slug aimed at it hits dodgeFactor times as often and costs the fleet dodgeDeltaV Mm/h of speed change (fuel). It stops dodging when its supplies fall below dodgeStopsBelow of full, to keep fuel to get home.
combat._spreadComment: Spread fire: each railgun fires slugsPerGun slugs at once in a fan fanMm wide at the target (focused fire: focusFanMm), each hitting accuracy times as often, then the guns cool for cooldown reloads. A sidestep (dodgeFactor above) barely helps against a fan (sidestepVsSpread). A hard burn dodges harder: hits x hardVsFocused against focused fire and x hardVsSpread against a spread, costing hardCost times the sidestep's fuel per slug. A dodge needs time: slugs fly at slugSpeedMmPerHour plus the closing speed, and a dodge only works fully when a slug takes fullDodgeSeconds or more to arrive, less the closer and faster the shooter.

_sensorsComment: Passive sensors only. A sensor sees a fleet out to sensorMm x sqrt(signature). A fleet's signature is its largest ship's signatureSize, plus a quarter for each other ship, times the factor for what it is doing: cold (drifting or coasting, engines off), orbit (holding orbit with small thrusters), warm (coasting within warmHours of a burn: the engines are still hot) or burn (main engines firing). With these numbers a frigate sees a cold frigate at about 30,000 km (so cold ships can still creep inside missile range), a warm one at 1.5 million km and a burn at about 9.5 million km; a home planet sees five times as far (a burn about a third of an AU away). Planets block the line of sight. Your shipyard planet, and any body with a sensor station, sees out to planetSensorMm; other bodies you hold see like a destroyer (planetBareSensorMm). Sightings no longer updated are forgotten after forgetAfterHours.
_lightComment: Light lag. Signals and orders travel at speedKmPerSecond (real light speed), times the game's light speed setting. Each side commands from its flagship; fleets within commandRangeAu of it count as live, with no lag.
_flagshipsComment: Cover and flagship hunting (light lag). A shot at a protected ship in a Screen fleet hits another ship instead with screenChance (closeChance in Close cover; escorts within escortScreenMm help screen). Point defence kills pdProtectFactor times as many missiles aimed at protected ships (closePdFactor more in Close cover) and pdOtherFactor for the rest. Close cover makes dodging closeDodge as useful. A ship not fired at for unshotHours aims unshotAccuracy times better. Watching an enemy fleet builds a flagship score per hour: signalPerHour from signal traffic if it carries the flagship (tightBeamLeak of that with Tight-beam comms, none in radio silence) and coverPerHour if it guards a protected ship; suspected at suspectAt, at most maxGuess; out of sight it fades by decayPerHour. A close look confirms or clears it.
_dronesComment: Messenger drones carry orders to a fleet a planet cuts off from the flagship: they fly at speedMmPerHour straight to it (round anything in the way), cost Industry, and hand the orders over within reachMm. An enemy fleet with railguns within shotRangeMm shoots one down at killPerHour (a chance of killPerHour x the hours it stays in reach). At 20,000 Mm an hour (about 2 % of light speed) a drone crosses an AU in about 7.5 hours.
_recordingComment: Battles are recorded to watch again from News: a frame every frameMinutes of battle, thinned out past maxFrames; only the latest keepBattles keep their frames.
_heatComment: Heat (per ship, up to its class heatCapacity). Gained per hour: idlePerHour always, burnPerHour with main engines firing; perRailSlug per slug fired; perDodge per slug dodged (times up to dodgeCloseMax the closer the shooter is inside railgun range); heatPerShieldPoint per point a shield soaks. Shed per hour: radiateOutPerHour with radiators out, radiateInPerHour with them in (in battle on Auto, or running Cold). Past capacity a ship overheats: radiators forced out, railguns and shields off, point defence at overheatPdFactor, until it cools to recoverAt of capacity. A fleet running Cold (radiators in, engines off) has signature x coldSignature. Radiators out in battle: hits do radiatorsOutDamage times the damage. A heat sink dumps sinkHeat at once (auto at autoSinkAt of capacity, or when missiles are within decoyMm); thrown hot, it draws off each missile closing on that ship with decoyChance (decoyBrain2Chance for brain 2). Shields (class shield x research) soak missile damage in full and railgun damage x shieldRailFactor, recharging shieldRegenPerHour of full per hour. Long-range railgun fire reaches longRangeMm at longAccuracy (falling to nothing at the far end), reloads longReloadFactor slower and never hits a dodging fleet. Firing at engines: hits x enginesHitFactor, and a hit knocks out the engines with enginesModuleChance. Held missiles launch at midLaunchMm or closeLaunchMm; a missile arriving with fuel left cuts the target's dodge by up to heldDodgeCut, its point defence by up to heldPdCut and the chance a heat sink fools it by up to heldDecoyCut. Dropped missiles drift dark until their timer (at most dropWaitHoursMax), then go for any enemy ship within dropSeekMm.
_formationsComment: Formations: railguns need a clear line (a fleet-mate within blockMm of the line of fire, between shooter and target, blocks the shot); missiles launch over friends. Point defence counts fully for fleet-mates within pdCoverMm, pdOutsideFactor beyond. A ship whose shield is down takes shieldShare of each hit on the shield of a fleet-mate with shield emitters within shieldCoverMm. The fleet re-forms when its front turns more than turnRadians. Auto picks Wall when at least wallMissileShare of the ships are missile boats and one has wallHeavyArmour or more.
_weaponsComment: Plan 3 build 2 weapons and counters. lance: a pulse lance mount fires a beam every reloadSeconds out to rangeMm; it can't be dodged, hits with accuracy (falling to half at full range), does damage and pushes heatToTarget into the target (shields soak the damage but take shieldHeatFactor times the heat); each shot heats the firing ship by heatPerShot, so lances overheat a ship fast. mines: laid one per missile from the racks (defensive-mines research), at most maxPerLay a ship; a field round a planet sits planetRadiusMm above its surface and moves with it, a field dropped in space is radiusMm wide and drifts at the layer's speed x dropSpeedShare, spreading by driftMmPerDay (thinner as it grows) until lifetimeDays. A ship crossing a field is hit with hitChancePerMine per mine (thinned by spread, at most maxHitChance) for damagePerMine; a field you know about (seen within spotMm, or struck by it) is crossed with knownCut fewer hits, and a fleet with point defence holding inside a known field clears sweepPerPdHour mines per mount per hour. Without IFF codes a field hits its own side's ships too. strikeCraft: a fighter base keeps squadrons (fighters and bombers) that sortie at enemy fleets within rangeMm of the planet, at most every sortieHours. Bombers hit for bomberDamage each; each squadron in the sortie can be lost to the target fleet's point defence (lossPerPd per working mount, at most maxLoss; fighters escorting cut it by escortCut). Fighters hit for fighterDamage, cut bombing of the planet by fighterBombShield each and kill fighterMissileKill of missiles aimed at ships in orbit. A lost squadron is rebuilt after rebuildDays for rebuildAlloys from the planet's store. counters: jamming leads jamByBrain[brain-1] of the missiles that get through off target (dumb ones ignore it); hijack (missile-hijack research) takes over hijackByBrain[brain-1] of guided missiles within hijackMm and turns them on their own side (dumb brain 1 missiles have no receiver to take over; IFF codes on the launching side cut it by iffHijackCut). secrecy: holding back fires at hideRangeShare of true reach until advanced weapons come out, which they do when any ship falls below belowHull of its hull or the odds drop below oddsBelow. rivalTech: ideas the rival fields are learned (Seen, then Studied at studiedAt, Unlocked at 1) by battleTeach per battle they are shown in, wreckTeach per wreck stripped, captureTeach per ship captured, planetTeachPerDay for each rival building seen on a colony; an Unlocked idea costs unlockedCut less time and needs none of its prerequisites.

sensors._extraShipComment: Each ship past the first adds extraShip of the largest ship's size (engine glow and heat); a lone ship running cold shows only soloCold of its size, so a single raider can sit in a lane long before it is seen.
sensors._identifyComment: Counting ships is easy once a fleet is in sight; telling which class each ship is (and so what it carries) needs a close look: within identifyMm of one of your fleets or planets (longer with sensor research).
sensors._cueComment: A fleet already seen leaves a predicted track. Sensors that know where to look see cuedFactor times as far, as long as the fleet is still within cueRadiusMm of where it was predicted to be, plus cueGrowthMmPerHour for each hour since it was last seen (it may have burned). The same holds a contact already in sight, so a fleet near the edge of spotting range does not flicker in and out. A fleet never seen, or one that changed course well off its track, gets no help.
